assignments.name: Homework: Graph traversal planning
assignments.description:
SYNTHETIC HOMEWORK. Prepare your own explanation of breadth-first search using an undirected graph with edges A-B, A-C, B-D, C-D. Start at A; visit neighbors alphabetically.

  1. Describe the queue after each visit and give the traversal order.
  2. Explain why the running time is O(V+E).
  3. Compare one limitation of breadth-first search and depth-first search.

Concept explanations and clearly labelled reference examples on a DIFFERENT graph are permitted. Do not turn generated reference material into a submission. Cite the course graph-traversal notes and identify uncertainty.

rubric.description: Time complexity explained using vertices and edges
Breadth-first and depth-first trade-offs with source attribution

materials.title: Graph traversal: queues, paths, and complexity
materials.content: Breadth-first search uses a FIFO queue and marks each vertex when it is discovered. Each vertex enters the queue at most once. With adjacency lists, all incident edges are scanned once per endpoint, so the running time is O(V+E). Breadth-first search finds shortest paths in an unweighted graph. Depth-first search uses a stack or recursion and explores a branch before backtracking. Worked reference graph: edges P-Q, P-R, Q-S; start at P. The traversal order is P, Q, R, S. This is a reference on a different graph, not a submission to the synthetic homework.
